summary: Best-of-4 RAG temps, Swift coverage select
hypothesis: Sampling RAG-augmented drafts at multiple temperatures and picking the best by coverage should outperform a single-temperature RAG call, because diversity across temperatures should surface a set that spans more question dimensions.
technique: Four RAG-retrieval + generate calls at temperatures [0.3, 0.6, 0.9, 1.0] produce four candidate question sets; a deterministic Swift scorer (weighted dimension-span across budget/timeline/scale/location/current-state with redundancy and "how many"-already-stated penalties) selects the highest-coverage set.
result: Scored 0.245 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 9 losses vs Sonnet), down −0.075 from exp003 and −0.062 vs baseline; rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3 — discarded. Coverage did not improve (still 3), and high-temp sampling actively degraded atomicity and specificity in ways the keyword-only Swift scorer could not detect, confirming the hypothesis was falsified: a coverage-only proxy ruler backfires when it cannot penalise compound questions or generic framing.
